title: Zero-Dependency AI Agent Harness Construction in TypeScript: Provider-Agnostic Loops, Workspace Jailing, Atomic Batch Budgets, and Seeded Failure Testing
author: Gabor Koos (freeCodeCamp, 2026; synthesized by Brain Harness)

claims.assertion: A production-grade AI agent harness can be constructed with zero framework dependencies in TypeScript using a provider-agnostic Model interface, structured run outcomes, and strict ReAct loop boundaries.
claims.source: Gabor Koos: 'How to Build an AI Agent Harness from Scratch in TypeScript' (freeCodeCamp, 2026)

claims.assertion: Passing unvalidated LLM-generated arguments directly to tools is a severe vulnerability; tool arguments must undergo pre-dispatch schema validation, and tool runtime errors must be strictly bifurcated from terminal model provider failures.

Filesystem sandboxing cannot rely solely on the final target path; robust path confinement requires canonical realpath resolution, lexical boundary checking, component-by-component ancestor lstat walking to reject intermediate symlinks, and O_NOFOLLOW file open flags.

Allowing models to formulate raw shell command strings or select arbitrary executables permits command injection; agent command execution must be locked to developer-defined presets with shell: false and bounded output buffers.

Tool invocation budget enforcement must occur atomically before conversation transcript mutation; admitting partial tool batches or appending assistant calls before budget verification creates orphaned, unfulfilled tool calls.

Sliding context windowing must treat each assistant turn and all its corresponding tool result messages as an indivisible atomic unit, preventing conversational incoherence from orphaned results or broken tool-call links.
Telemetry and observer listeners must be wrapped in isolated try-catch boundaries so that non-essential reporting errors never fail or alter the outcome of an otherwise successful agent execution.
